Book a walkthrough with our team. Book a walkthrough FAQ Frequently asked questions. How the Jenz platform works, what it connects to and how your data is protected. Book a demo What is Jenz? Jenz is an AI platform for commerce teams. It connects to the systems your store runs on and gives the team one workspace to ask questions across all of your data, build apps on live numbers and automate recurring work. The Jenz agent works inside that platform and takes on tasks for the team, in the tools you already use. What are Jenz apps? Apps are internal tools that Jenz builds from a plain description. Ask for a view of which products will sell out and when, your real margin per product after freight, fees and ads, or revenue per campaign, and Jenz builds it on your live data and keeps it current. Apps can be shared with the team, and they can include actions, such as approving a reorder or pausing a campaign, directly from the app. How do automations work? Any recurring task can be turned into an automation: the Monday sales report, a daily stock check, invoice matching or a scheduled newsletter. You describe the routine once, approve the steps and set the schedule. Jenz runs it the same way every time, reports back when it is done and records every run. When the same request comes up more than once, Jenz offers to automate it. What does the Jenz agent do? The agent is the part of Jenz your team works with directly. Tag it in Slack or Microsoft Teams, or reach it by email, WhatsApp or iMessage, and it carries out the task with the context of the conversation: pulling numbers, drafting customer replies and product copy, analysing ad performance or preparing a reorder. It also monitors the business and raises issues before anyone asks, such as a product about to sell out or a campaign losing money. Which systems does Jenz connect to? The systems a commerce business runs on, including Shopify, WooCommerce, Stripe, Klaviyo, HubSpot, Meta Ads, Google Ads, TikTok, Zendesk, Gorgias, QuickBooks and Xero, and more than 3,000 other apps through the integration catalogue. Connections use your own accounts and can be revoked at any time. If a system you depend on is not listed, raise it in the demo. How is Jenz different from ChatGPT or Claude? General assistants only know what you tell them in each conversation. Jenz is connected to the business itself: it reads your orders, stock, ad accounts and finance data, retains decisions and context over time, runs work on a schedule and builds tools the team keeps using. It runs on the same frontier models, inside a platform designed for operating a store. How do we stay in control? You decide what Jenz may do on its own. By default it prepares the work and asks for approval before acting, and anything that affects spend, stock or customers keeps an approval step until you remove it. Every action, app change and automation run is logged. Does Jenz improve over time? Yes. Jenz maintains a private memory of your business: products, suppliers, margins, channel performance and the decisions the team has made. As it repeats work, it records how your team wants each task done, so results align more closely with your processes every week. Memory is scoped to your workspace and never shared with other customers. How is our data protected? Each customer has an isolated workspace, and every task runs in a sandbox only your workspace can reach. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, hosted in the EU or the US at your choice, and never used to train AI models. A Data Processing Agreement is available to every customer, and full details are on our Security page. Which AI models does Jenz use? Jenz runs on frontier models from the leading providers, and you choose which one. The model can be changed at any time without affecting your apps, automations or connections. How do we get started? Book a demo. We review your store and the work you want to hand over, connect your systems together with you and agree on the first apps and automations. Pricing is based on how much work Jenz carries out for you, and we cover it in the same call. Your store, run by agents . The company is two people. Jenz runs the weekly reporting, demand forecasting, the product catalogue and the SEO and content work, so the two of them can spend their week on the shops. The situation An unmanned store has nobody behind the till, but the office work does not go away. Somebody has to read the sales numbers for four points of sale, keep the shelves and the webshop stocked, write the articles and newsletters that bring people in, and answer customer emails. With two people, that work got squeezed. Articles went out when there was time, and the weekly numbers got a quick look rather than a proper read. What Jenz does 01 Weekly reporting Sales, cost, bestsellers, footfall and conversion for all the stores and the webshop, with what changed since last week and why. 02 Demand forecasting Per SKU and per location, built on sales history, seasonality and supplier lead times. Jenz flags what will sell out before it does and drafts the reorders and pre-orders. 03 Catalogue from supplier lists Jenz reads the supplier price lists, matches every line to an existing SKU or creates a new one, and updates stock, cost prices and product data in the store. 04 SEO strategy Keyword research and search trends turned into a plan: which terms to rank for, which pages to build, and a content calendar that follows the season. Every month, a report on what moved. 05 Articles and newsletters On a fixed schedule. The team picks the topics. Jenz writes, adds images and publishes. 06 Customer enquiries First-line replies, ready for the team to send. The result The reporting, content and purchasing work now runs with about an hour a week from the team, mostly spent choosing topics. Some of that is time they no longer spend. Most of it is work they would never have got round to: a proper weekly analysis, and two to four articles a week, which they did not have the people for before. “ We run three unmanned stores and a webshop with two full-time staff. Jenz gives us a weekly analysis, regular content and better purchasing: work we would otherwise have had to hire for. The biggest win is not just the time, but that we make better decisions faster. ” André Pedersen Founder and CEO, Go On Shop Norge Next customer story How Titanbar hands 90 hours of work a month to Jenz.
